note: Examples for the schema, not game content. A play is a life's signature verb: what a farmer does that nobody else can.

items.title: The harvest gamble
items.setup: The barley is ripe a week early and the sky to the west has the look it had the year the Tolls lost everything. Cut now, green at the edges, and sell what you get; or leave it a week for the full head and pray the weather holds. {spouse.name} says cut. The old man at the mill says wait.

stages.text: Seven days of looking west. The head fills. The sky does what it will.

words.good: the weather held and the head filled
words.bad: the rain came on the sixth day and lay the barley flat

success.title: A full head
success.text: You waited and the sky waited with you. The barley came in heavy, and the price at the market was the price for a full head, and {spouse.name} said nothing about having said cut.

failure.title: Laid flat
failure.text: The rain came on the sixth day and lay the barley flat, and you cut it wet off the ground and lost a third to the rot. The old man at the mill did not look at you for a month.

stages.text: The grain is in. Sell at the autumn fair, or hold it in the barn for the spring price and the rats.

words.good: the spring price was high and the rats were few
words.bad: the spring price fell and the rats did not

success.text: Held the grain for the spring price and won.

failure.text: Held the grain for the spring price and lost it to the rats.

items.fallout: A farmer who gambles on the weather twice and loses twice is a farmer the village lends to carefully. The old man at the mill has a word for it, and uses it.
